newsitem.title: USA: BRE Properties buys Calif. unit for $23.5mln.
newsitem.headline: BRE Properties buys Calif. unit for $23.5mln.

text.p: BRE Properties Inc said on Monday it bought Sycamore Valley, a 440-unit apartment complex in Foundation Valley, Calif. for $23.5 million in cash.

BRE Properties said in a statement it acquired the multifamily property using tax-deferred proceeds from recent sales of non-core assets, and that the property was expected to achieve a first-year yield in excess of 9.5 percent.
Sycamore Valley had a 98 percent occupancy rate, BRE said.
BRE Properties President and Chief Executive Officer Frank McDowell said in a statement the REIT was continuing to expand its portfolio and dispose of non-core assets.
"We continue to expand the apartment portfolio through a strategy that benefits from a sharply defined regional focus, yet is not overly dependent on any one market," McDowell said.
The Sycamore Valley acquisition would increase BRE's presence in the Los Angeles/Orange County area to seven communities with 1,598 apartments.

"BRE remains on track in its growth strategy with substantial funding available from a continuing orderly disposition of the company's non-core assets," McDowell said. "In the last 90 days, BRE has sold eight non-apartment properties for an aggregate $87.2 million."
McDowell said in the same period, BRE used about $66 million in sale proceeds to by three apartment communities with a total of 1,138 units.
BRE has also committed to using $13 million of the proceeds to buy 240 more units under development in the Phoenix, Arizona area.
